text: The type is a dependent finitely supported function space, with additive operations coordinatewise. This realizes [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22)’s direct sum and extends the same construction to additive commutative monoids. Infinite index families are allowed; each individual element still has finite support. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L38).

Bijectivity of the canonical summation map means exactly that every ambient element has one finite expression with a term from each summand. This expresses the internal direct decomposition used in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). An empty family is internal only when the ambient additive monoid is trivial. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L440).

The fields supply a two-sided inverse to canonical summation, hence the unique finite homogeneous decomposition of every element. This is explicit data for the internal direct sum in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). It excludes unrelated equivalences by fixing recomposition to the summand inclusions. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L55).

Bijectivity supplies an inverse to canonical summation, and its two inverse laws give the required Decomposition fields. This selects the components of the internal direct sum in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). The source proves Decomposition is a subsingleton, so the mathematical components do not depend on the choice. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L79).

The left-inverse law makes canonical summation surjective, and the right-inverse law makes it injective. Thus a supplied decomposition gives precisely IsInternal. This is the existence-and-uniqueness description of the direct decomposition in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21), valid already for additive commutative monoids. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L87).

The two displayed composite equalities say summation followed by decomposition, and decomposition followed by summation, are identities. Evaluating them gives exactly the Decomposition fields. This constructs the canonical direct decomposition of [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21); both inverse directions are required. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L70).

The forward map returns the finite family of components, and the inverse sums their inclusions into M. The supplied inverse laws make this an equivalence, matching the internal decomposition in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). Additive and linear structure are exposed separately by the corresponding bundled equivalences. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L92).

The predicate requires membership to be preserved by every canonical component projection. For an additive subobject this is equivalent, by finite reconstruction, to being the sum of its intersections with the pieces, as in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). The definition itself also accepts arbitrary SetLike subsets without assuming closure. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L101).

Every element is a finite sum of homogeneous components. A predicate containing zero and all homogeneous elements and closed under addition therefore holds everywhere. This is induction on the finite decomposition in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21); the explicit zero case also covers an empty index family. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L105).

Canonical summation is additive and bijective, so its inverse is additive too. Bundling that inverse yields M≃+⨁ℳᵢ with the same components as decompose. This is the additive decomposition underlying [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21); no additive inverses in M are needed. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L158).

For submodules, canonical summation is R-linear, so the inverse of its bijection is R-linear. The result packages exactly the existing decomposition and its recomposition, as in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). The argument uses no division or subtraction and retains the stated semiring generality. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Decomposition.lean#L260).

Spanning makes canonical summation surjective, while independence over a ring makes finite component expressions unique and hence makes it injective. This characterizes the internal direct sum in [Hazrat §1.2.1–2](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). Ring and AddCommGroup are explicit; the independence-to-injectivity implication is not asserted for arbitrary semimodules. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L519).

Scalars act coordinatewise on the finitely supported family. Since scalar multiplication preserves zero, support remains finite, and each module law follows coordinatewise. This is the module structure used in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22), with the same construction valid over any semiring. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L42).

The docstring calls this an “embedding,” but the map need not be injective: for two copies of the full additive submonoid of ℕ, the distinct families (1,0) and (0,1) both map to 1. `coeAddMonoidHom_of` confirms these values. The definition correctly gives the canonical summation homomorphism; the docstring should say “homomorphism.” See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L409).

This sends a finite family of submodule elements to their sum in M, exactly [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22) applied to the subtype maps. It is R-linear, and its range is the sum of the submodules. The definition correctly makes no injectivity or spanning assumption. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L402).

The value on a finite family is Σᵢφᵢ(xᵢ), the unique map specified by [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). The source confirms its restriction to each summand and uniqueness among linear maps. Finite support makes the construction valid for arbitrary index sets and semirings. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L107).

This inserts x into coordinate i and zero into every other coordinate, as the canonical summand inclusion in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). The construction preserves addition and scalar multiplication, and evaluation at i is a left inverse. DecidableEq supplies the index comparison. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L79).

The induced map sends coordinate xᵢ to fᵢ(xᵢ). Zero preservation keeps the support finite, and linearity holds coordinatewise. This is the map obtained from [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22) by composing each fᵢ with the corresponding target inclusion; no injectivity or surjectivity is assumed. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L249).

Coordinatewise injectivity implies injectivity of the whole family map. Conversely, insert two elements into one summand and use its injective inclusion to recover injectivity of fᵢ. These are the canonical inclusions in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). The equivalence also holds for an empty index family. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L270).

The right side consists exactly of finitely supported target families whose i-th coordinate lies in range(fᵢ). Choose preimages only on their finite support and use zero elsewhere to obtain a direct-sum preimage. This follows the finite-support construction in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22), without requiring every fᵢ to be surjective. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L292).

The equality e⁻¹(I)=J lets the induced map [h]↦[e(h)] have source H/J, by [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [forward](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L323) and [inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L334) squares pass. Equality of ideals, rather than one inclusion, ensures this is an isomorphism; proof transport leaves the canonical map unchanged.
Explicit ideal-matching equality transport preserves the forward quotient square.
Inverse ideal-matching quotient square agrees with the ambient inverse.

Both composites send h to the class of e(h) modulo I, agreeing with [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The equality hypothesis identifies J with e⁻¹(I), so equality transport has the correct source. The published [inverse-square control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L334) passes and verifies the opposite direction with e.inv.
Inverse ideal-matching quotient square agrees with the ambient inverse.

Quotienting by zero identifies [h] with h; the forward map lifts the identity and its inverse is the projection, as in [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Published [forward](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L381) and [inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L388) controls pass. The two composites are identities because the projection is surjective and has zero kernel.
Zero quotient is identified by the lift of the identity.
The inverse zero-quotient isomorphism is the quotient projection.

The inverse H→H/0 is exactly h↦[h], consistent with the zero-ideal case of [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [forward-map control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L381) passes, identifying its inverse with the lift of the identity. This states equality of Hopf morphisms, not definitional equality of the quotient object and H.
Zero quotient is identified by the lift of the identity.

Surjectivity identifies H/ker(f) with the entire target K, via [h]↦f(h), as in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Published [forward](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L401) and [inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L411) controls pass. The kernel uses the surjective constructor, so this ring-base statement requires no flatness. Surjectivity is required to identify the entire codomain.
First-isomorphism forward factorization recovers f.
First-isomorphism inverse sends f(h) to its source quotient class.

Projection followed by the kernel-quotient isomorphism sends h to f(h), the factorization in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [representative-evaluation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L226) passes. The equality concerns morphisms H→K and retains f’s surjectivity, which supplies the isomorphism rather than merely a forward quotient lift.
The kernel quotient lift evaluates as f on representatives.

The inverse first-isomorphism map sends f(h) back to [h], as in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [forward factorization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L401) passes; composing it with the inverse yields the displayed identity. Different preimages differ by ker(f), so the target is H/ker(f), not a chosen section into H.
First-isomorphism forward factorization recovers f.

If I≤J, every element of I vanishes modulo J because the projection kernel is exactly J, the quotient convention of [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [induced-map control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L472) passes. The inclusion points toward the larger ideal’s kernel; reversing it would not give a well-defined map H/I→H/J.
Nested-quotient map sends [h] modulo I to [h] modulo J.

The inclusion I≤J makes [h] modulo I map to [h] modulo J by [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Published [evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L472) and [uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L532) controls pass. The direction is from the smaller ideal’s quotient to the larger ideal’s quotient; the map need not be injective.
Nested-quotient map sends [h] modulo I to [h] modulo J.
The nested quotient factor is characterized uniquely by its composite.

Every class modulo J has a representative h, and its class modulo I maps to it by [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [class-evaluation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L472) passes. This proves surjectivity of the underlying coordinate function; it does not assert injectivity, a splitting, or surjectivity on algebra-valued group points.
Nested-quotient map sends [h] modulo I to [h] modulo J.

A class [h] modulo I vanishes modulo J exactly when h∈J; hence the kernel is J’s image in H/I, by [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Published [evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L472) and [injectivity-boundary](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L561) controls pass. The surjective kernel constructor permits the general ring base without flatness.
Nested-quotient map sends [h] modulo I to [h] modulo J.
The nested quotient map is injective exactly when I=J.

Over a field the flat-kernel constructor agrees with the surjective kernel, giving ker(H/I→H/J)=J/I, consistent with [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Published [constructor comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L191) and [zero-kernel boundary](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L561) controls pass. The Field hypothesis supplies the required flat modules; it is not silently generalized to arbitrary nonflat kernels.
Surjective and flat kernel constructors agree when the flat hypotheses apply.
The nested quotient map is injective exactly when I=J.

Both composites send h to its class modulo J, the factorization required by [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [three-ideal composition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L551) and [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L543) controls pass. Category composition applies the projection modulo I first; the containment I≤J is exactly what makes the second map well-defined.
Nested quotient maps compose along I≤J≤K.
Equal ideals produce the identity quotient map.

This packages H/I with its descended Hopf structure and inherited finite generation, matching [Mathlib’s finite-type quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/FiniteType.lean#L94). Images of finitely many algebra generators still generate the quotient. Published [zero-quotient](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L723) and [kernel](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L628) controls pass. Finite presentation, Noetherianity and finite generation of I are not assumed.
Finite-type zero-quotient forward isomorphism is the identity lift.
Forgetting the finite-type projection gives ordinary kernel I.

The canonical H/0≅H from [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78) lifts to the full subcategory of finite-type Hopf algebras. Published [forward](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L723) and [inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L620) controls pass. The object-property wrapper restricts objects by algebraic finite generation and imposes no additional condition on these Hopf morphisms.
Finite-type zero-quotient forward isomorphism is the identity lift.
Finite-type zero-quotient inverse is the canonical projection.

The underlying map remains the canonical projection H→H/I from [Mathlib’s Hopf quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Quotient.lean#L37); finite generation makes its target an object of the full subcategory. Published [forgetful-map](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L602) and [vanishing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L633) controls pass. The wrapper changes neither the quotient ideal nor the direction of the coordinate morphism.
Finite-type projection forgets to the original Hopf projection.
The finite-type projection kills precisely the elements of I.

After forgetting the finite-type wrapper, [h]=0 holds exactly for h∈I, the quotient convention of [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [ordinary-kernel control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L628) passes. Finite generation does not alter the equivalence, and the ideal is I itself rather than its radical; nilpotents outside I remain visible.
Forgetting the finite-type projection gives ordinary kernel I.

The ambient isomorphism induces H/e⁻¹(I)≅K/I by [h]↦[e(h)], as in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Both quotients remain finite type by [Mathlib’s finite-type quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/FiniteType.lean#L94). Published [forward](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L692) and [inverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L705) squares pass. The full-subcategory wrapper preserves the original Hopf maps and the preimage-ideal convention.
Forward finite-type quotient transport square commutes.
Inverse finite-type quotient transport square commutes.

For I≤J, the ordinary Hopf quotient lift [h]↦[h] from [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78) is a morphism between finite-type quotient objects. Published [evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L755) and [composition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L788) controls pass. The full-subcategory construction adds no new morphism condition and keeps the direction H/I→H/J.
Finite-type nested quotient sends a class modulo I to its class modulo J.
Finite-type nested quotient maps compose along ideal inclusions.

Every class modulo J is the image of the same representative’s class modulo I, as in [Milne, Proposition 3.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [finite-type evaluation control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Quotient/Basic.lean#L755) passes. The assertion is surjectivity of toBialgHom on coordinate elements; finite generation neither changes the function nor implies an inverse for strict ideal containment.
Finite-type nested quotient sends a class modulo I to its class modulo J.

Joined x y is existence of a continuous path on [0,1] with precisely those endpoints. Nonempty hides the chosen path, rather than requiring a distinguished one or a unique homotopy class. Constant paths, reversal and concatenation supply the expected equivalence relation. Compared with [p.17, path definition; pp.19–20, path components](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L62).

The witness path must remain in F at every time, including both endpoints. This matches a path in the subspace F. It correctly fails when either endpoint is outside F; it is therefore not reflexive on all of X unless F=X. Compared with [pp.9–11, subspaces; p.17, paths](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L175).

The chosen point lies in F and can be joined within F to every other point. Reversing and concatenating these paths gives the usual pairwise condition. Mathlib deliberately includes nonemptiness, so this is Hatcher’s path-connectedness condition on nonempty subspaces, not its vacuous empty-set extension. Compared with [p.17, pairwise path-connectedness; p.19, reversal and concatenation](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L412).

The fields state nonemptiness and existence of a path between every ordered pair. The path condition is standard; the explicit Nonempty field records Mathlib’s convention, which is stronger on the empty space than Hatcher’s bare pairwise formulation. It asserts no local condition or chosen system of paths. Compared with [p.17, path-connectedness definition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L577).

This is the set of points reachable from x by a continuous path in X. The source’s component-path construction keeps every intermediate point in this set, and maximality is expressed by inclusion of any path-connected set containing x. It is a path component, not necessarily a connected component. Compared with [pp.19–20, definition and maximality of P(x)](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L291).

Membership means reachability from x by a path wholly inside F. Thus it is the relative path component when x∈F. For x outside F the total definition gives the empty set, as the existing nonempty-iff lemma confirms; it does not silently adjoin x to F. Compared with [pp.9–11, subspaces; pp.19–20, path components](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L354).

The equivalence relation is on points of X: two points are related exactly when some path joins them. Its three laws use a constant path, reversal and concatenation. It does not quotient paths by homotopy; that would describe morphisms of the fundamental groupoid instead. Compared with [pp.19–20, decomposition by path reachability](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L112).

The type is points of X modulo path reachability, giving the unbased set π₀(X). It has neither a prescribed basepoint nor a group structure in this declaration. The surrounding source gives the quotient topology separately, without claiming that it is always discrete. Compared with [§8.1 p.57, π₀ as the set of path components](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [pp.19–20, path components](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L117).

The map sends x to its equivalence class under path reachability. Its fibers are precisely path components, and every class has a representative. This is the canonical projection X→π₀(X); it is not a choice of a point from each component or a selection of a connecting path. Compared with [§8.1 p.57, set of path components](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [p.42, canonical quotient map x↦[x]](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L125).

Path-connectedness is exactly having one path component. Nonempty and Subsingleton together express exactly one; Subsingleton alone would wrongly include an empty space. The reverse direction uses equality of quotient classes to recover a path between any two representatives. Compared with [§8.1 p.57, π₀ as path components](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf); [pp.19–20, path-component partition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L583).

The existential point x supplies nonemptiness, and pathComponent x=univ says that every point can be reached from it. Reversal and concatenation then join any pair. The statement correctly uses existence of such a point rather than a universal condition that would be vacuous on empty X. Compared with [pp.17 and 19–20, paths and component partition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L717).

Paths in the subtype F are exactly ambient paths whose entire range lies in F. Both sides also require F to be nonempty, so the equivalence handles empty sets consistently. No openness or local path-connectedness of F is required for its inherited subspace topology. Compared with [pp.9–11, subspace topology; p.17, paths](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L611).

A path-connected subset is connected in its subspace topology. Paths carry the connected interval into F, while the path-connectedness witness supplies the nonemptiness required by IsConnected. The declaration states only this implication; no converse or local path-connectedness is assumed. Compared with [p.17, path-connected implies connected; pp.20–21, converse counterexample](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L733).

The instance yields connectedness from path-connectedness, preserving the nonempty-space convention in both classes. Its source includes the whole path component in the connected component. This proves the intended one-way implication without asserting that connected spaces are path-connected. Compared with [p.17, implication; pp.20–21, failure of its converse](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L721).

The image f(F) is path-connected: applying f to a path in F gives a path in the image with the correct endpoint values. Surjectivity onto all Y is unnecessary because the conclusion concerns only the image. The source even has a stronger ContinuousOn version. Compared with [p.18, continuous-surjection proposition applied to the image; p.11, restrictions](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L446).

A point in U∩V serves as a common center: paths inside each set join it to all points of U∪V. The explicit nonempty intersection is the needed bridge. Neither set has to be open, and the intersection need not itself be path-connected. Compared with [pp.17 and 19, path definition and reversal/concatenation; direct union consequence](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L522).

For x∈F, its relative component is nonempty and is path-connected within itself. The source uses truncated initial segments to show that every point along a witness path remains in the same component. Merely knowing that its endpoints lie there would not establish this conclusion. Compared with [p.19, initial-segment argument for intrinsic path-connectedness of P(x)](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L511).

A continuous surjection sends a path-connected source to a path-connected target. Source paths project to paths between any target pair, and surjectivity also transports nonemptiness. Continuity and surjectivity are separate explicit premises; no quotient-map, openness or lifting property is needed. Compared with [p.18, continuous-surjection proposition (b)](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L623).

An arbitrary equivalence-relation quotient of a path-connected space is path-connected with its quotient topology. The canonical projection is continuous and onto, so its image paths suffice. There is no separation or openness condition on the equivalence classes. Compared with [p.18, continuous-surjection proposition; pp.41–42, quotient topology](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L632).

The binary product is path-connected by pairing paths in X and Y at the same time parameter. The product topology makes this paired path continuous, and nonempty factors make the product nonempty. This is a direct consequence of the cited product-continuity criterion and path definition. Compared with [p.13, continuity into a product; p.17, path definition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/Top/TopNotes.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean#L675).
